utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Brix Andersen. Just for the record, my name is Stephen Sayers, and together with my colleague, Mr. Naumovski, we represent Dario Kordic. These gentlemen to the rear of me are Mr. Kovacic and Mr. Mikulicic, who represent Mario Cerkez. I take it, sir, that you were interviewed by the Prosecution two days ago and that you signed a statement on that date, November the 28th, 1999; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also authenticated a significant quantity of documentation, by my count close to 800 pages. Could you just let us know when those documents were provided to you for your review?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were provided on Sunday and Monday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now, you have stated in your direct testimony that you had never met or spoken to Mr. Kordic and you have never been to Central Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would be accurate to say that all of the assessments, conclusions, and opinions that we heard from you yesterday are based upon the conclusions, opinions, and observations of others lower down in the organisation of which you were a member in 1993, the European Community Monitoring Mission; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I had no personal knowledge of what happened in Bosnia, as a governor, but as to the sources, yes, my information was based on what was reported to me by the ECMM monitors and the RCs but also from the information received from the presidency and UNPROFOR and other sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But just so the record is crystal clear, you yourself had no independent personal knowledge of any of the facts relevant to what was happening in Central Bosnia or the facts that are recited in your assessments and records; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I have no -- I have no personal access to facts as such in Central Bosnia. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can leave that subject now, Mr. Brix Andersen. Would it be fair to say that as a career diplomat, sir, of many years experience and training, you are taught to be and are careful when you make written conclusions, when you write written conclusions?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Both written conclusion and statements in other forms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree that it is important to ensure the factual accuracy of the materials upon which you rely to make sweeping conclusions about someone that you have never met or spoken to? Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason is, of course, that if the facts upon which you base the conclusions are not correct or inaccurate in any way, then obviously that affects perhaps vitally the validity of the assessments, opinions, and conclusions that you write; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me just ask you if you have ever met or spoken to any members of the HVO leadership, and I'll mention some names to you. I'll just represent to you that Dr. Jadranka Prlic was appointed president of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, on the 14th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll similarly represent to you, sir, that on the same day, Stipo Ivankovic was appointed vice-president or the first vice-president of the HVO. Have you ever met or spoken to that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of October, 1992, some few months later, Kresimir Zubak was appointed the second vice-president of the HVO. Have you ever spoken to or met that gentleman, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same day as Mr. Zubak was appointed vice-president of the HVO, Anto Valenta was appointed a vice-president of the HVO too. Have you ever met or spoken to him, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a reference in your April the 17th to 18th, 1993 report -- I think it's dated [sic] Z735 -- to the head of the HVO department of defence, a man by the name of Bruno Stojic. I believe he was appointed on June -- in June of 1992 to that position. Have you ever met or spoken to Mr. Stojic, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Have you ever met or spoken to the president of an entity known as the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, a man by the name of Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just step back a little bit, sir, and ask you some general questions about your understanding of what was going on in Central Bosnia during the time that you were responsible for your duties in the European Community Monitoring Mission headquarters in Zagreb. I believe that we've established that your duties basically spanned the first six months of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there from August, beginning of September, 1992, as a monitor, and with a view to preparing the Danish presidency; that is, setting up the organisation that we would run when we took over from the British. Then I would stay on as Deputy Head of Mission from the 1st of January. So from the 1st of January through June, 1993, I was the Deputy Head of Mission. Before that I was the regular monitor and head of the Danish contingent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please forgive the pause, Mr. Brix Andersen, but we have to let the interpreters catch with us. There is no doubt, sir, that throughout the time of your involvement in the former Yugoslavia, from August of 1992 up until the termination of your position as Deputy Head of Mission in Zagreb at the end of June of 1993, that there was a vicious ethnic civil war raging throughout the territory; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Court knows we have a continuing objection to the characterisation in questions as a "civil war." We haven't renewed it often but just to make sure that it's on the record, we object to the characterisation in question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's ultimately for us to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not sure really if it assists us, who have to decide that ultimate question, to hear it described as a civil war or not. Mr. Sayers, I would say this: that it's a question in similar terms which you've put to virtually all the witnesses. I myself now can't see the point of it, because clearly there was a war raging, and if the next question is was it chaotic and confusing, you can take it that it was. We don't need to hear that repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am mindful of those observations and I'm also mindful of the observation that the Court made some days ago regarding repeating territory over which we've already trodden, but the purpose of this question for this particular witness, since this witness has been offered to speak with the voice of the ECMM, was not really to elicit his personal opinions but, rather, to elicit the view of the ECMM. I can confirm that with an ECMM document that I think outlines the view of the ECMM, and I'd just like the witness to confirm that, with the Court's permission, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, you can put the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This has already been admitted. It's Exhibit Z1040, and I have an additional copy there to be shown to Mr. Brix Andersen for his convenience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wonder, Mr. Brix Andersen, if you would turn to page 9. Perhaps it might be useful to have a copy for the ELMO, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The document, Mr. President, is dated June the 10th, 1993, and it appears to be entitled, "Excerpts of Political Material in ECMM Team Reports."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just like to read to you one section, sir, in the third paragraph. It says: "It is beyond doubt in this area," and that's Busovaca and Novi Travnik, "that a war which began as a common fight against a common foe (the Serbs) has degenerated into an outright civil war." And that is the view of the ECMM at the time of this particular document, June the 10th, 1993; isn't that so, Mr. Brix Andersen?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps not quite, in the sense that if you look at the first page of this document, it's entitled "Excerpts of the Political Material in the ECMM Team Reports." Now, that means that this is the unedited observations and statements by the individual teams. It was at the time thought to be useful to us in headquarters to have the unedited opinion of the monitors on the ground. So this would not have passed through the CC or the RC chain of command to headquarters. This would be the raw material written by the team leader and his fellow monitor. So this does not necessarily represent the opinion of the ECMM headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what was the opinion of the ECMM headquarters? Was it a civil war or wasn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that question bears on the legal qualification of the events in the former Yugoslavia, and I think it is up to the Court to decide what the qualification should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree, sir, that the situation that confronted you in the former Yugoslavia was a disintegrating country that had emerged from a single-party system?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To my recollection, there was one dominant party, but there were other parties as well. That's besides the point perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia, there's no question that there was a tradition of an omnipresent, all-powerful central government; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is certainly correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the early '90s, immediately before the foundation of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on March 6, 1993, there's no question that that central government had disintegrated, at least in the territory of the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And really before the central government of the republic was able even to start functioning, Sarajevo had been surrounded and besieged, had it not, sir, in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you know, that was before my time with the ECMM. That is certainly common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And there is no question, sir, that throughout your tenure or throughout the time of your responsibilities for Central Bosnia, the central government in Sarajevo was really not able to communicate effectively with other parts of the country; in effect, it really was not functioning at all, was it?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government obviously could not function the way a western government functions today, but to take it to the extent that there was no communication between the government and the territory I think is carrying it a bit too far. There was communication. The members of the leadership and the government were able to travel, with assistance from UNPROFOR and others from time to time, but I don't think it's correct to say that they were limited to Sarajevo without communication to the rest of the country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree, though, that the government of a country effectively could not function, and the result of that was that communities and peoples were basically left to organise and fend for themselves?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I will stick to what I said in answer to your previous question. Yes, there was a government. Yes, they were doing what they could to exercise control. Yes, they were facing difficulties, more difficulties than most other governments would face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Have you actually ever heard of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what it was, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard of it. I had a general impression of what was the gist of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the powers of a vice-president of the Croatian Community --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, I wonder what the point of asking the witness this sort of question is. If you have a case about what the powers were, it may be simpler if you put it to the witness so that he can comment on it as to whether he knew or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's a fair observation, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was actually the supreme commander of the armed forces of the HVO, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the exact functioning of the various persons who were in the Herceg-Bosna leadership, I would hesitate now, six years later, to have any precise opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opinion at the time in 1993 or did you not know?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew what was the main area of responsibility of most of the important persons, but to say that I could describe it in legal detail, no, I don't think I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic was the chief of the general staff of the HVO, the senior commanding officer of the military forces headquartered in Mostar, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware that the military organisation of the HVO was split into various operative zones under the command of separate subordinate commanders subordinate to Brigadier Petkovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, that in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, you were aware that the military commander was Colonel Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that appears to be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one final question on personalities and whether you had met them. Did you ever meet Bozidar Rajic, the Minister of Defence of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and a vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection that I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brix Andersen, was the ECMM ever aware that the HVO was established as a temporary emergency measure until some semblance of civilian order could be restored in the country?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's a difficult question to answer, because most of what happened in the former Yugoslavia was of a temporary nature at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good point. Let me just ask you to take a look, if you would, at a document that's already been introduced into evidence. I don't think it's in your bundle, but it comes from the ECMM archives, and I think it was one of the documents that you were brought here to authenticate. It's Exhibit Z1132, and it appears to be a document entitled, "Excerpts of Political Material in ECMM Team Reports," dated June the 28th, 1993. Before we actually go into this document, had you left your duties by that date or were you still performing your duties, sir? That's June 28th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still there at that time. We left, I believe, on the morning of the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we have it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. I'll put page 4, which is the only page I wish to ask the witness about, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Basically, sir, this is the second page of a report from the coordination centre in Mostar, and it records a meeting with Mr. Vlado Pogarcic, who was the advisor for foreign affairs for Mr. Mate Boban. Basically, there are a number of points recorded that are made by Mr. Pogarcic. The one I want to draw to your attention is on page 4, which says: "HVO/HDZ always said that Community of Herceg-Bosna is a temporary solution to allow to establish normal life again. It will disappear as far as there is an overall solution." The question that I have for you is, sir: is that basically consistent with the ECMM's understanding of the functions of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the HVO, as a temporary solution in an emergency?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, these reports are unedited, in the sense that they contain the material reported directly from the teams of the CCs. Now, as to the substance of it, as I said before, everything was temporary in the former Yugoslavia. There had been a number of peace plans put forward by Mr. Akmadzic, by Mr. Vance and Owen, so everything in that sense was temporary. Everybody was hoping for a solution to the whole conflict, so in that sense, yes, temporary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no more questions on that document. As there was a reference to the HDZ, did you have any knowledge of who held what post within that political party, sir, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had that knowledge in 1993. Obviously, six years later, it will be difficult to say with certainty what was the exact nature of that knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir. All right. With respect to Mr. Kordic, let me just ask you some questions about him. I would like to begin with what you described as your valedictory analysis dated June the 16th of 1993, marked Z1065, and I think that's in your bundle. The only particular reference to Mr. Kordic appears on page 4, paragraph 16, which you have already read into the record. Is it true, sir, that the factual information contained in this paragraph is based, would it be fair to say, entirely on the reports of Jean-Pierre Thebault to you, the head of the regional centre in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not. It would be based on his reports and his assessments but also the assessment of other people, other organisations, like most of what we did in headquarters, we did not rely exclusively on one source. We tried to balance information we received with information from other sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I explained with the mission of the three ambassadors who went to Ahmici, yes, we did rely on Mr. Thebault to be a competent and meticulous head of the RC, which never meant that we would not find it useful to have his information and his assessment corroborated by other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. I wonder if I could just ask the usher to put one page of Exhibit Z840 on the ELMO. Page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the comments section of Mr. Thebault's April the 28th, 1993 memorandum, sir, he informs the headquarters of the ECMM that Mr. Kordic is, in fact, the cousin of Mr. Boban. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the ECMM ever came up with that notion?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Let me put it a different way. Let me suggest to you that Mr. Kordic is, in fact, not Mr. Boban's cousin and is not in any way related to him. Can you tell us or do you know where the ECMM came up with that erroneous factual information?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. It was reported to us, and it was a fact that we never questioned; not to my knowledge, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on -- thank you. I'm through with that document. I appreciate it. You make the contention in paragraph 16 of your valedictory memorandum that Mr. Kordic is supposedly, "Minister for Herceg-Bosna in the HVO government." What does that mean, sir? Minister of what?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's fair to say that for many of the people holding responsible positions in Herceg-Bosna, it was difficult to have a precise description of their titles. They would tend to differ from time to time. Some of it could be changed, changes made in the leadership. Some of it could be changes because of translation errors. Some of it -- I don't know. Basically, this is taken to mean that he held a responsible position. Whether it was "minister" in our sense of the word or whether it was a leading personality was not of any great importance for the thrust of this paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, sir, that -- and I'll suggest to you that, in fact, Mr. Kordic was never minister for Herceg-Bosna and that he held no position in the HVO government. Could you just tell us where this information came from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information came to us from the reports from the RC's and from the teams. If you say it's inaccurate, I really have no other comment to that, other than Mr. Kordic's name repeatedly came up in reports from the field, from other sources also, as an influential person. Whether he held this or that title is perhaps, to me, not quite as important as the importance of his position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Do you know, in order to clear up this confusion, apparently, as to the status and functions of Mr. Kordic in Central Bosnia, do you know whether anyone actually asked him what his position was and what his powers were?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. A number of ECMM monitors must have met him. I suppose that they would have had the opportunity to ask him the question if they felt it was a relevant question to ascertain his formal, precise title. Perhaps they also had the opinion, but I'm speculating, that the fact that he seemed to exercise authority was sufficient for them when they were discussing things with him, rather than to ascertain his exact legal title. I don't think I can comment any closer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And I don't mean to quibble, but the long and the short of it is you just don't know whether anybody asked that particular question of Mr. Kordic himself, do you?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly, you don't know whether anybody took the trouble to ask the question of the head of the HVO government, Dr. Jadranka Prlic, what functions, if any, Mr. Kordic had in that government? You don't know, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for a fact, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the political front, the same is true with respect to Mr. Boban, the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and also the president of the HDZ. You do not know whether anyone within the ECMM took the trouble to ask him what Mr. Kordic's functions or powers were, do you?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like I said just before. We were less concerned with the formal legal title of the people we were dealing with, the same as we within the ECMM actually had very few titles and very few titles were used. It was a question of mostly the authority that the person seemed to exercise. If you were an influential person, then that would be sufficient for us to talk to him or relay his views and the information he would give to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate the repetition of that answer, Mr. Brix Andersen, but the question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think the question has been put often enough. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On the military front then, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anybody questioned the military authorities in Central Bosnia, Colonel Blaskic, for example, as to whether Mr. Kordic had any military power whatsoever, and if so, the extent of it or the limitations on it? You don't know that, do you?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the highest level, the same is true with respect to the commander in chief of the HVO armed forces, Brigadier Petkovic. You don't know whether anybody clarified with Brigadier Petkovic whether Mr. Kordic had a military role and, if so, what was it and what limitations were attendant to it; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be fair to say, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me turn to a different subject, sir. Mr. Anto Valenta, about whom you gave some testimony and whose name is mentioned in the ECMM reports and who was, in fact, a vice-president of the HVO, his name is actually mentioned in Exhibit Z859,1. It's a May the 1st, 1993 special report, and I believe it is in the package that you have in front of you. If you would just turn to it, sir. I actually have --

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have the reference, again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's Z859,1, sir, and May the 1st, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There are just two pages that I would like the usher to put on to the ELMO, if I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first page is page 2, sir, of this special report, and it's right at the bottom of the page where the reference is made that: "Mr. Valenta, HVO vice-president, located in Travnik where he took a decisive part to the recent troubles, just before the conflict." Then there's a reference to Mr. Kostroman, who is supposedly or who is described as: "General Secretary of the HVO travelling the area." Do you know what kind of decisive part in the recent troubles Mr. Valenta took? Was that ever reported to you or do you have no current recollection of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If would you turn to the second page. It's under paragraph 3, "Provisional conclusions." It appears on page 6, I believe, of this document. There's a reference, in the first full paragraph of this letter, if you would just -- yes. To a letter that had been sent or: "Very clear letter sent the week before to the ECMM by an HVO vice-president, who is the real number two, after Mate Boban, of the HVO as a political body, Mr. Valenta." Supposedly, the author of this special report was to meet with Valenta that afternoon, as he was just coming back from a town called Citluk, where he had played a major role as the HVO representative in charge of the situation in Central Bosnia. This is what was reported to you by the head of the regional centre in Zenica in May of 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of any information to suggest that the assessments and conclusions contained in this document are factually incorrect, are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You describe two documents in connection with your direct testimony. Thank you, I'm through with that. The first was a fact-finding mission report that was generated, I think, by three Ambassadors. It was Exhibit Z910 and dated May the 12th. I don't think we need to put this one on the ELMO. I'll just touch very lightly on this. Apparently the Ambassadors wanted to meet with the responsible local authorities to the extent that they could. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were sent there to see for themselves what had happened --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- form their own opinion and talk to the people necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. They were taken around by UNPROFOR; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken around by ECMM but with the escort of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you're aware, they spoke to everybody to whom they wished to speak in order to come up with valid conclusions regarding their fact-finding mission; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. I know that they have reported on the conversation they've had. I have no recollection that they had wished to see other people whom they couldn't see. They may have had other wishes which for practical or other reasons could not be met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware, sir, that they did, in fact, have a meeting with Mr. Valenta, the HVO vice-president; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware that they had no meeting with Mr. Kordic; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent -- if I can add that -- that it is not reflected in the report, and I have no recollection, six years later, whether or not they had met Mr. Kordic and not reported it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a very fair observation, Mr. Brix Andersen. You also made one reference to a report by Charles McLeod, Exhibit Z926. I only have one question in connection with this document. Mr. McLeod records that he -- "I went to the area to talk to leading members of the community on both sides." Are you aware, sir, that not only did Mr. McLeod not meet Mr. Kordic, he never attempted to meet with Mr. Kordic, never asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How is the witness going to know this sort of thing? It doesn't help us, and, anyway, we heard Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, the point is made and there is no need to beat a dead horse. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the documents that was contained in the package of materials that you were asked to review and authenticate, Mr. Brix Andersen, was Exhibit Z856,1, and it consists of three -- actually, two separate documents. It looks like there is a press release from HINA, the press agency [Realtime transcript read in error "president"] In Zagreb that you referred to. I don't know whether you have a copy in your package. The press release, and we'll try to locate a copy of this document just in a few seconds, the press release makes reference to a joint statement issued by President Boban of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and President Alija Izetbegovic of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on April the 25th, 1993, regarding the political and military situation in Central Bosnia. Do you recall whether you ever saw a copy of that joint communiqué?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if the usher would just show you the document marked as Exhibit D27/1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: While that's being located, Mr. President, I think there's one transcription error on line 7, page 25. The word "president" with the term "president agency" should read "press agency."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may or may not have seen this joint statement, Mr. Brix Andersen. There are actually two separate documents. There's a joint statement issued by President Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban, witnessed by Dr. Franjo Tudjman, and then at the end there is a separate document regarding the command structure for the BiH army and the HVO, signed by the commanders in chief, President Izetbegovic, and Mr. Boban, and by the military chiefs of the general staffs of both organisations, General Sefer Halilovic and General Milivoj Petkovic. Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have, but I wouldn't say it with one a hundred per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The --

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say I believe I have, then it is because the information there would have been known to me somehow. Whether it is based on these documents it's impossible to remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have for that. If you have no clear recollection of it, then there's no point in going through the document, Mr. Brix Andersen. One document would I like you to look at and verify for us though is this document that was attached to Exhibit Z856,1. Unfortunately I only have one copy of it so I'll put this on the ELMO, please. Do you recognise this document as a press release issued by the HVO public relations office on May the 1st of 1993, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've seen it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the faxed information that's contained on the top of the first page, is it accurate to say that this document was being faxed within the ECMM to its various offices, to people that needed to see it? I believe the fax date appears as May the 3rd of 1993.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The information I can see seems to indicate that this document was sent from the ECMM to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Copenhagen. The acronym UM KRYPTO, that is the name of a fax machine in Copenhagen. So it was sent from Zagreb to Copenhagen, it appears to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only point that I would like you to confirm or deny, as the case may be, is that this document was in the possession of the ECMM by May the 5th of 1993 at the latest?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would have been there on the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I wonder if the usher could just show you page 2 of this document. Paragraph 4. Were you aware that the HVO public relations office, sir, I believe in Mostar, had announced to the world at large that an investigative commission would be appointed to investigate the facts regarding the crimes that had occurred in the recent past in the interethnic fighting that had broken out in Central Bosnia and else where?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning, when I say I remember that, yes, I remember seeing it in this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. I'm through with that. The next topic I'd like to address is the ceasefire negotiations, Mr. Brix Andersen, that actually brought something of an end, perhaps a lull, in the fighting that occurred in Central Bosnia. Were you aware that the head of the regional centre of the ECMM in Zenica was a participant in those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those negotiations occurred on the highest military level, did they not? Perhaps that's an unclear question. Let me --

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the translator. Yes, I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Participants in those negotiations included not just the head of the regional centre in Zenica but also the commanding officer of UNPROFOR in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Lieutenant-General Philippe Morillon; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the most senior military officers on the part of the competent factions, Brigadier Petkovic for the HVO, General Halilovic for the ABiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that you actually -- did you actually write a memorandum about those negotiations yourself, sir, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the briefing notes I used in Geneva?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a good place to start. You actually did make a reference to the ceasefire negotiations in your briefing notes and briefed, in the document that you prepared, for Lord Owen's use; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document Lord Owen used was much later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection, that was in the first third or first half of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on, sir, but just ask you to agree that Mr. Kordic took no part whatsoever, as far as you're aware, in any of those ceasefire negotiations or any of the original ceasefire negotiations that occurred in Vitez involving representatives of the HVO and ABiH sides.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you a precise answer to that. No, I don't have any recollection of it today. It doesn't mean it did not happen. It may not have been reported to me or I may have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just don't know; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on in time, you made a reference to a meeting held at Medjugorje on May the 18th of 1993. Do you recall that? Once again, sir, it's true that all of the principal civilian and military leaders on both sides were present at that meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, including my own minister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Kordic took no role whatsoever in any of those negotiations, did he, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. It was not reported to me that he did. He may have been there without it being reported.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, though, you simply don't know whether he was there or not, so you can't help us out on that subject, can you?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One general question concerning a body known as the Busovaca Joint Commission. Have you ever heard of that body or does that not ring any familiar bells in your recollection?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that as far as you're aware, Mr. Kordic took no role whatsoever in the negotiations that were chaired by one of the ECMM monitors, Mr. Jeremy Fleming, I believe, that led up to the establishment of that body; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct I have no recollection of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you -- were you aware that Mr. Kordic -- not only did he not take any role in those negotiations, he never sat on the Busovaca Joint Commission at all and never attended a single of the daily meetings held by that institution?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether he was there or was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he were there, it would somehow have been reflected in the reporting, I'm confident, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Let me move on to another topic. You were asked some questions in connection with Exhibit Z943,2, which was a two-page document. It looks like it's signed by Torbjorn Junhov. I think that's in your package, and it is dated the 19th of May, 1993, regarding the relations between Bosnian Croats and Muslims and application of the agreements that had been worked out at Medjugorje. Just one point of detail on this, since this document shows essentially how the Vance-Owen Plan was supposed to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just for the Trial Chamber's information, I had previously pointed out Exhibit Z571,1, pages 138 to 39, and that was in the testimony of Brigadier Duncan. There's no need to go over that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would it be fair to say, sir, that as of this date, the governmental arrangements envisaged for Province 10 under the Vance-Owen Plan, the Travnik or Travnicka province, were as follows: The provincial governor was to be a Croat; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask me detailed questions like that, I think my answer would be I have no recollection over and beyond what is in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In that case, I would just like to draw the Trial Chamber's attention to the bottom of this page which deals with Travnik and providing that the governor would be a Croat, the vice-governor would be a Muslim, and that the interim provisional government would consist of five Croats, four Muslims, and one vacancy. If you have no knowledge of this document, sir, we will move on, but just one point of detail. Do you know who the provincial governor was supposed to be, the Croat provincial governor?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection now. I may have had at the time, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a reference in Exhibit Z1013, a special report dated June 3rd, 1993, on page 2 that says: "The mayor of Bugojno, Mr. Seljic, HVO, has now been appointed as governor by the Bosnian Croats, and it seems to everybody, including the Bosnian Muslims, to be a good beginning." Does that refresh your memory at all?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaguely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is true that Mr. Soljic was supposed to be the Croat governor of Province 10, as far as you're aware; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the document here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brix Andersen, do you recall the ECMM ever receiving any reports concerning the structure of the military forces in Busovaca and the chain of command within those forces?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not offhand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. With respect to the document about which I was just asking you some questions, there's a reference, sir, to high political and military leaders from the Croat and Muslim side being present, namely President Izetbegovic, Mr. Boban, Mr. Ganic, and a gentleman by the name of Mr. Akmadzic. Does the name "Akmadzic" ring a bell? Do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does ring a bell, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that Mr. Akmadzic was one of the five vice-presidents of the HDZ political party?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was envisaged, sir, that a military committee consisting of President Izetbegovic, Mr. Boban, Mr. Ganic and Mr. Akmadzic would be formed; correct? If you take a look at page 2 of the document that we were just discussing, Exhibit 943,2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts should the witness look, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On page 2, Your Honour. It's rather difficult to read because the copy is a little blurred, but it appears under Roman Numeral V, "Central Government." It's May the 19th, 1993, sir. I have a copy for the ELMO, if that would assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would just look down at Roman Numeral V, sir, it says, "Central Government. It was agreed that in accordance with existing constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the following changes should be made: A military committee of four should be established," and it contains the four names that I just recited. It also goes on to say that those members affected would have to resign their positions and that it was further agreed that Mr. Prlic would be appointed the prime minister of the government. You were aware that Mr. Prlic was actually the president of the HVO at this time, were you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, thank you. The next document that I'd like to just ask you a few questions about is Exhibit Z993, Mr. Brix Andersen, May the 29th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I have a copy for the ELMO, Mr. President, if the usher would be so good as to put it on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first page to which I would like to draw your attention is actually page 7. Once again, sir, this is an official ECMM document; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document in a series of briefings prepared by the headquarter staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so this sets out the position of the ECMM headquarters on the date of this document, anyway, the 29th of May, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you turn to page 7, paragraph 8, sir? One question about this. The observation is made by the ECMM headquarters that: "While the Vance-Owen Plan may be the preferred solution for the West, it may falter in attempts to impose it on a region where the natural political evolution may be toward three constituent states." That was the view of the ECMM at the time this document was prepared; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not. As I said, this was a briefing document prepared for the headquarters. Now, this did not reflect, shall we say, the official position of the ECMM as we would report it to headquarters. This would be more a sort of discussion paper for our internal understanding of the situation. This was not supposed to be made public. It was not supposed to be sort of a background paper for policy decisions. This was how we saw it, and this was how we thought it would be useful to stimulate the monitors' thinking about what was going on on the ground. So it does not reflect European policy on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, we were still committed to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan. What it says here is that it would be a difficult job, which it has also proved to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This does represent what the headquarters was disseminating to monitors as briefing materials; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We disseminated this to monitors for their information, not as a policy statement that the Vance-Owen Plan was about to fall. On the contrary, at every given opportunity we declared that we were firmly behind the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan. But we could also see what was happening in the real world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's true that the plan actually evolved in July and August of 1993, as far as you're aware, into the Stoltenberg-Owen Plan which actually did envisage a union of three constituent republics of three constituent peoples; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as you indicate, this is after I had left the mission, so I didn't follow events quite as closely as when I was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are aware of the basic details of the Stoltenberg-Owen Plan, and that's about the most basic detail; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Next, sir, page 7 again, paragraph 10. The observation is made by the headquarters that the rise of nationalism among the peoples of this region has created what are arguably legitimate aspirations for self-determination and sovereign state status. Then you go on to observe the challenges that are connected with that particular observation. Was that the view of the ECMM at this time at the end of May 1993?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was our assessment that there was a rise of nationalism. I think that very few people would doubt that. I think also that it is true that what had been created was what was arguably legitimate aspirations. That goes for all of the peoples in the former Yugoslavia, for the Krajina Serbs, for the Serbs, for the Croats, for the Croatians, for the Muslims. What we tried to grasp was how do we explain to ourselves and to the outside world exactly where is the limit. The view of the mission was that we would try to understand what were the political motives behind the events on the ground, while at the same time being very careful not to accept or condone the methods with which the peoples of the region tried to implement these political principles. So we tried to make a clear distinction between our analysis of the political aspirations and the methods of the leadership and the methods of the troops and the people on the ground. I think that is, in essence, what the mission was about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But never accepting the methods which were not democratic, legitimate, in every single aspect of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware, I take it, at all times, sir, that the Croat segment of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina was a small minority, about 17,3 to 17,8 per cent of the total population; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Total population of what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Total population of what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina, the republic.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are many statistics. It depends a little on when you make the census. Yes, we were aware that the Croat community was fairly small when you compare it to the total population of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Yes, we were also aware of the fact that in Herceg-Bosna, there was a majority. But I don't think it's fair to ask if I remember all the figures to the exact point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we had the basic understanding of the figures for the whole of the country and for the various provinces, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two final questions in connection with this document, sir. If the usher would turn to the next page, page 8, there's a summary prepared by Mr. Pugh from the information section. The conclusion appears here that there is a separate but parallel agenda that exists among all three parties to this conflict. Do you have any knowledge of what that agenda was or what the discussions on the subject of that tripartite agenda were?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the fair answer to that question is that whenever we were dealing with events in Yugoslavia, you wouldn't expect one agenda only from any given party. There would always be one extra or several extra agendas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you found that to be the case with respect to all of the various participants in the conflict; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a general statement, yes, like I just said, but depending on the level at which you are operating and the territory which was involved. There was never any clear agenda, one agenda, for each of the parties, covering all aspects at all levels and all territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can I just draw your attention, lastly, on this document to paragraph 14. There's a rather resigned tone about that paragraph, which indicates that the ECMM's view is that: "The Vance-Owen Plan, while still the official international solution, may not be able to be implemented because of the deep-rooted animosity among the warring parties, and the capacity to live together may simply not exist." Was that the official ECMM view at the end of May 1993?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. And we were right, weren't we. But with the added comment that the official position of the ECMM was to work for the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan until the day that Lord Owen himself declared it didn't serve any purpose any more and you had to start afresh. So we were loyal to the political directives we received from the presidency and from the Member States, but it didn't mean that we did not think about what we saw on the ground ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was there a perception on the part of the ECMM that UNPROFOR, the UNPROFOR forces in Central Bosnia, were not able to function at full effectiveness because of the tremendous limitations upon their mandate, being confined, as they were, to providing assistance to the UNHCR in the provision of humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're putting it more squarely than I would subscribe to. I think UNPROFOR was doing their very best to implement their mandate as they construed it. They were facing great difficulties, which was obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your valedictory address, June the 16th, 1993, Exhibit Z1065, on page 7, you make the observation that: "The current conservative interpretation of the mandate limiting UNPROFOR to support of UNHCR convoys has given the impression of an ineffective organisation and has deeply affected the credibility of the International Community." Then you make some suggestions regarding a possibly more expansive interpretation of UNPROFOR's mandate. But the conclusion that I've just read to you, that's a conclusion that you had reached at the end of your tour, essentially in the middle of June of 1993, is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that this is a conclusion I signed on to in a report to my government. I think it's fair to say that if I had written the same paper for publication, I would perhaps have termed it slightly different, but in a sense it would be the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The final topic that I would like to cover with you, sir, and I appreciate your patience, is the testimony that you gave regarding the asserted presence of Croatian army units or forces in southern Bosnia-Herzegovina. You never saw any reports of the presence of HV or Croatian army troops in Central Bosnia, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have the reports before you. I was not a monitor in the field in this period of time. We used not a lot but we used some of the resources of the ECMM in order to ascertain whether or not the HV were operating inside Bosnia or whether they were giving support, in terms of equipment or supplies, to the HVO. As is stated in several of the reports, it was, of course, difficult to find such information because, obviously, it would be in the interests of the HVO and especially the HV to try to keep it concealed to us and UNPROFOR. Nevertheless, it was our considered opinion that the HV did give assistance to the HVO. If you go back to the paper regarding the Medjugorje meeting, it would be difficult for us or for the West to tell President Tudjman that he should limit the support and that he should exert influence on the HVO if we thought that Croatia did not assist the HVO. And this was done on behalf of the European presidency, it was done by the president himself, my Foreign Minister, and was done with the knowledge of all the member governments. Now, if our information had been inaccurate, there would have been one or more of the member states whose representatives would have objected to this statement being made. The fact that the presidency was able to make the demands --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I going to cut you off, sir. I appreciate your answer but the question is a very narrow one. You never saw any reports of the presence of HV or Croatian army troops in Central Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness cannot be expected to remember everything that's in the reports. As he points out rightly, you have them. Now, if there's any further point you want to make about it, do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have been provided with three reports. Let's take a look at one or two of them, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sayers, yesterday you said that you would finish this cross-examination this morning. Moreover, it is a cross-examination based on the examination of certain documents. You have been cross-examining the witness for about an hour and a half, and I really should like to know -- I would appreciate you telling me how long do you intend to go on, bearing in mind that Mr. Kovacic also needs to cross-examine this witness. So how long will you take do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm mindful of the commitments I made to the Trial Chamber yesterday. As I informed the Trial Chamber, this is the last subject about which I have questions for Mr. Brix Andersen, and I would anticipate maybe another 20 minutes of questions and I'll be through. So Mr. Mikulicic will have the remainder of the time, which should be a good hour and a quarter, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can look at the documents -- we'll adjourn, take our break now -- and reduce it to 10 minutes if it's merely one subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I just raise an administrative query at one stage this morning in order to plan witnesses for this week and next week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be convenient when we've completed this witness. Yes. Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brix Andersen, we've been given ten minutes, so please give me a hand. We'll try to rush through these three exhibits in short order. The first is Exhibit Z1151,1, and I have a copy here for the ELMO. This is a document dated July 30, 1993, and I appreciate that this postdates your involvement in the area, sir. But if you take a look at the first page, the observation is made that it is very difficult for ECMM teams to provide a definite answer to these questions, questions such as HV involvement in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as military intelligence is strictly forbidden to them for their safety in the field. That was true throughout your tour as deputy head of the mission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We were very concerned about the security of our monitors. We were unarmed and we were not able to protect ourselves. Therefore, we made a point of being seen -- not only being but being seen to be impartial, and to engage in intelligence gathering would not be impartial. But there is a difference between intelligence gathering and providing information on what is obvious on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But suffice it to say that it was the position of the ECMM that it was difficult for monitors to gather military intelligence for the reasons stated in this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We would try to get the information from the ground that occurred, but we would not go to the extreme that a military unit perhaps would go in order to obtain such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could just draw your attention to the second page, sir. If you could just lower the page, Mr. Usher, by about two inches, actually lower it instead of pushing it up. There you go. Now, would it be fair to say, sir, that the best that the ECMM had accumulated as of July the 30th, 1993, on this subject, HV involvement in BiH, were the hints or evidences in three areas of Herzegovina summarised on this page?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six or seven years later, I don't think I can provide any more specific information than what is in the document here, over and above to say that it was an issue in which we took great interest. We wanted to be able to verify to our governments whether or not Croatia was involved, so we went to some lengths in order to obtain such information without endangering our personnel. And we were quite confident that the Croatian government, the Croatian army, did operate within Bosnia-Herzegovina with equipment, with personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never obtained any definitive information regarding the magnitude of that involvement, though, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not over and above what is in the reports in evidence here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, moving along -- I'm finished with that document -- the next one that I would like to address to you is Exhibit Z1012 about which you gave testimony. This is a document dated June the 3rd, 1993. I have one question on page 1. If you go under -- Mr. Usher, if you could show paragraph 2, please, on the ELMO. Thank you. That's good. There's a reference here to a trickle of confirmed proof, and as of June 3rd, 1993, the position that the existence and extent of HV involvement has always been difficult to define, and the many reports provided by the BiH Armija have seldom been confirmed by ECMM, UNMOs, or UNPROFOR, and that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but you must also understand again that we did not get involved in what is strictly intelligence gathering, and it wasn't necessary for our purposes. Our purpose was only to demonstrate that there was a high degree of probability, bordering on certainty, that the Croatian army was involved. That was enough for us to report to the presidency and to the capitals that there was a problem which we couldn't solve on the ground and which would be an issue that should be dealt with at the level of capitals and for capitals to decide whether or not to approach President Tudjman or others in order to stop such assistance. Now, we didn't have to provide specific information on where and when we decided particular pieces of equipment or troops, but our assessment was, and it still stands, that there was HV involvement in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with that document, and the last document that I have for you is Exhibit Z1050, which is a document dated June the 13th, 1993, and about which you testified, sir. This is right at the end of your tour, and as you've stated in your direct examination, part of the mission of the monitors on the ground was to look for proof of HV involvement specifically. In Item 7, the observation is made that regardless of the outcome of the debate over HV presence in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the international perception is as you've or as this document articulates. There is no question that there was an active and ongoing debate about the nature, existence, or magnitude of the involvement of HV troops in south-western Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that we started to debate within the ECMM the extent to which there was HV presence and assistance. We did not discuss and we did not doubt among ourselves that there was such an involvement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The debate, though, was still unanswered as of this date, was it not, June the 13th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not. The debate would have been over, at the very latest, in preparing for the Medjugorje meeting. At the Medjugorje meeting, the presidency explained to President Tudjman that the time had come to stop HV involvement. These statements were on the basis of several reports, of course, to the presidents in Copenhagen and to capitals, but one of the sources would, of course, be the ECMM, and at that point in time there was no doubt about Croatia's engagement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one question in that regard, sir. With regard to paragraph 5 of this document, apparently there had been a discussion between the headquarters of the ECMM and Major General Slobodan Praljak from the Croatian Ministry of Defence, and it was reported by Major General Praljak that while -- he denied that there was any direct involvement by HV combat forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And reported to you that people in HV uniforms may have been spotted but those were the individuals who were chosen to join the HVO for personal reasons; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that that is in the report. It was not our assessment that it was a true representation of the facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question, meeting the 10-minute deadline: Do you know whether the ECMM ever prepared any written analysis containing the conclusions that you've just reached, that the reports of involvement of Croatians on behalf of the Croat forces in south-west Herzegovina, for personal reasons, was, in fact, not true?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific recollection of any document over and above the documents that have been brought into the court as evidence here, but still, it was the general assessment of the ECMM headquarters, as well as the monitors on the ground, that there was such involvement. Now, sometimes you come to a point where you do not dispute the facts and you do not dispute the assessments. So over and above the documents you've seen here, there was no need perceived to prepare any specific analysis of the subject. We took it for granted. And the behaviour and the reactions of the various individuals was, in a way, to confirm our assessment. The document you pointed out here seems to confirm it, and the reaction of the Croatian government seems to confirm it. There was no dispute of the fact, there was no Member Government which responded to Copenhagen that ECMM was out of line, which would have been the case if we had made an erroneous assessment of such an important issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you're aware, the three documents which we've just looked at basically set out and summarise the sum total of information available on that subject, HV involvement in Bosnia-Herzegovina, south-west Herzegovina specifically, available to the ECMM after the conclusion of your six-month tour in Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not. These documents are the documents which have been brought before the Court. There may be other documents in the files of the ECMM. There may be other documents in the files of the Member Governments. These documents are there. There may be other information. You cannot conclude from my statement that this is all the ECMM knew about the HV involvement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If such documents exist, however, you certainly weren't shown them in preparation for your testimony yesterday and today, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was shown the documents which are in the folder here and which have been referenced to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, sir. I appreciate your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. No further questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Brix Andersen. I am Goran Mikulicic. I'm a lawyer from Zagreb, and with my colleague Mr. Kovacic, I represent the second accused in this case, Mario Cerkez. Mr. Brix Andersen, the ECMM headquarters in Zagreb where you discharged your functions was, if I may put it that way, a multi-national, multi-ethnic organisation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there are people who came from different countries, members of the European Union. Would it be then correct to say that members from different countries, members of the European Union, also brought with them different views about the situation in the then Yugoslavia, which would correspond, which would be in agreement with the official positions of the countries they came from?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would not be correct to say. If you came there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people were assigned by their governments. They came to the ECMM with their own background and experience. We were under the command and control, whichever word you prefer, of the ECMM headquarters. They were briefed on the situation by the ECMM over and above whatever national briefings they may have received. They were not there to represent national political points of view. Some of them, from countries which had had close relations to one or the other of the parties, would have the advantage of perhaps understanding better the situation. Some of them even spoke the language, which of course was an advantage. But, no, they were there as monitors. They were under our control. They did not represent the Member Nations. That level of control was exercised through the presidency which rotated with the European presidency. So whatever political input had to come from capitals would come via the presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I quite understand that, Mr. Brix Andersen, but as you say yourself, there were different people with different backgrounds coming from different cultural environments and different levels of education too. So would it be fair to conclude that when on the ground those people, of course, acquired and developed their own views, of course within the broad context of the monitoring mission?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to be splitting hairs with you, but it's very much a question of your definition. No, they did not have their own personal views. They had the views of the mission. They had -- you have to remember also that the teams always operated with at least two people. There were always two monitors on a team, plus a driver, plus an interpreter, but there were always two monitors. They would very seldomly be from the same country. They would prepare their reports together. So for one monitor to influence a report in a direction which was not based on the facts of the points of view expressed to them during conversations would be very, very difficult. So we made a special point of trying to ensure that all the monitors were impartial, and we didn't have any incidents of the kind you were referring to, where reports were obviously influenced by personal belief or national instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. Would this same conclusion could be applied vice versa too; that is, I mean, the briefings of the new monitors who would arrive in Zagreb and take over the functions. So that is, were the briefings on the ground just as well balanced when this comes to the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ECMM was set up very much like a military organisation, which it was not, but about 75, 80 per cent of the monitors were military men or women. And when things are done the military way, it is done very meticulously and it is down according to format. So there would be very little chance of any briefer to express and to impress on the monitors he was briefing his own personal points of view. It would be done on the basis of standard material with very little diversions from time to time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mikulicic, I should like to ask Mr. Andersen if when those monitors were briefed that what has already become international, but were those also asked to distinguish between the facts they reported and the opinions that they may have held or come to on the basis of what they had seen?
